response.basis: Reviewed all 13 numbered NL segments (NL1-NL13) against the primary typed plan's 38 contracts and 8 transition groups. Cross-checked containment obligations against the discourse-continuity rule for sibling operating alternatives under one common enclosing owner (AutonomousMode, HighwayMode, UrbanMode, CollisionAvoidanceSystem) and found each sibling substate introduced by a transition-endpoint clause lacked its own containment row in the primary plan, even where the group or endpoint contract existed. No ledger, score, or evaluation artifact was consulted; only the supplied numbered NL text and primary plan structure were used.
response.reason: The primary plan captured initial-entry, endpoint, guard, termination, and cardinality-relevant obligations thoroughly but systematically omitted many explicit substate containment relations that NL establishes alongside transition endpoints: (a) HighwayMode/UrbanMode as siblings under AutonomousMode (NL2), (b) cruise/lane_change as substates of HighwayMode (NL3), (c) lane_change_urban/straight/intersection as substates of UrbanMode (NL7), (d) exit_urban as a substate of UrbanMode first introduced in NL8, and (e) collision_avoidance_deactive/collision_avoidance_active as substates of the collision avoidance owner scope (NL12). Per the containment-preservation rule, a clause that both transitions into and structurally introduces a substate requires an independent containment contract even though endpoint/initial-entry contracts already exist for the same clause, and covered-segment status does not excuse omitting these. I also added one element_declaration contract for AutonomousMode itself as the root-level operating scope, since its existence as a distinct declared element is independently violable and was not directly represented by any primary contract (only its initial-entry and its containment of InitialState were captured). No new transition groups, endpoint, guard, event-consumer, action, or cardinality obligations were found beyond what the primary plan already represents; alternative destinations, guards, and lifecycle/termination properties for existing transitions are already fully covered by the primary contracts and its transition_groups.

No ledger, score, or evaluation artifact was consulted; only the supplied numbered NL text and primary plan structure were used.
arguments.reason: The primary plan captured initial-entry, endpoint, guard, termination, and cardinality-relevant obligations thoroughly but systematically omitted many explicit substate containment relations that NL establishes alongside transition endpoints: (a) HighwayMode/UrbanMode as siblings under AutonomousMode (NL2), (b) cruise/lane_change as substates of HighwayMode (NL3), (c) lane_change_urban/straight/intersection as substates of UrbanMode (NL7), (d) exit_urban as a substate of UrbanMode first introduced in NL8, and (e) collision_avoidance_deactive/collision_avoidance_active as substates of the collision avoidance owner scope (NL12). Per the containment-preservation rule, a clause that both transitions into and structurally introduces a substate requires an independent containment contract even though endpoint/initial-entry contracts already exist for the same clause, and covered-segment status does not excuse omitting these. I also added one element_declaration contract for AutonomousMode itself as the root-level operating scope, since its existence as a distinct declared element is independently violable and was not directly represented by any primary contract (only its initial-entry and its containment of InitialState were captured). No new transition groups, endpoint, guard, event-consumer, action, or cardinality obligations were found beyond what the primary plan already represents; alternative destinations, guards, and lifecycle/termination properties for existing transitions are already fully covered by the primary contracts and its transition_groups.

issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue UnspecifiedInitial is merely a synthesized stand-in and the semantic intent is obviously collision_avoidance_deactive; however the exact closed-model edge is the authoritative artifact under test and it does not reach the required target, regardless of author intent inferred from naming.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's owner-local initial pseudostate edge targets a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial placeholder instead of collision_avoidance_deactive

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.transitions tr_0006 (enter_hwy->cruise, event='dist_to_front<25 & extra_lane=true') and tr_0007 (enter_hwy->lane_change, event='dist_to_front<25 & extra_lane=true'); inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions transition:line:24 and transition:line:25 both triggers=[dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true] guard=null.
issues.expected: The cruise and lane_change alternatives from enter_hwy must be distinguishable by disjoint or otherwise separated guard/event conditions so exactly one branch is determinate under a given condition.
issues.observed: Both enter_hwy->cruise (transition:line:24) and enter_hwy->lane_change (transition:line:25) carry the exact same trigger event dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true with no additional guard, and the exact source inventory events for tr_0006 and tr_0007 are both 'dist_to_front<25 & extra_lane=true'. The two alternatives are not distinguished by any guard predicate.
issues.reason: NL3-DISJOINT-1 requires the cruise and lane_change alternatives from enter_hwy (group NL-GROUP-NL3-1, ALT-NL3-1 and ALT-NL3-2) to be distinguishable, but both share the identical guard 'dist_to_front<25 and extra_lane=true'; this is precisely the guard_disjointness violation pattern described in the routing discipline.
issues.requirement_quote: can transition to cruise or lane_change based on the distance to the front vehicle (`dist_to_front<25`) and the availability of an extra lane (`extra_lane=true`)
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue nondeterministic choice between cruise and lane_change under the same condition is an accepted design (the model may intend an underspecified nondeterministic branch), but this directly contradicts the NL's implication of a determinate/distinguishable outcome for each named condition.
issues.title: enter_hwy's alternatives to cruise and lane_change carry the identical guard/event, making them operationally indistinguishable

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions transition:line:71 source='[*]' target='UnspecifiedInitial' scope='CollisionAvoidanceSystem'; inspection_equivalent_facts.states shows UnspecifiedInitial as a distinct state at line 70 with reachable_from_initial=false; working_contract element compiler:state:...UnspecifiedInitial kind=synthetic_state; PlantUML source for CollisionAvoidanceSystem (lines 41-44) contains no [*] initial arrow at all.
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's exact owner-local initial pseudostate edge ([*] -> ...) must enter collision_avoidance_deactive.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM shows CollisionAvoidanceSystem's only owned initial edge is '[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial' (transition:line:71), targeting a compiler-owned synthetic placeholder state (state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:70) rather than collision_avoidance_deactive; collision_avoidance_deactive itself has no incoming initial edge.
issues.reason: The exact owner-local initial edge (owned by CollisionAvoidanceSystem) targets a different state (UnspecifiedInitial) than the NL-required target (collision_avoidance_deactive); this is a malformed nested initial edge per the malformed owner-local edge protocol, not merely an absent edge.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue UnspecifiedInitial is merely a parser artifact for an omitted PlantUML initial arrow and that author intent (collision_avoidance_deactive being 'initially' the state) should be read into it; however the working_contract explicitly classifies UnspecifiedInitial as a distinct synthetic_state (compiler:state:...UnspecifiedInitial) and the source PlantUML for this composite has no [*] --> line at all, so the exact closed-model edge is verifiably malformed relative to the NL-required target.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's owned initial pseudostate edge targets a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial placeholder instead of collision_avoidance_deactive

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text root scope only contains '[*] -> AutonomousMode : /Autonomous_mode_start;' with no edge to CollisionAvoidanceSystem; inspection_equivalent_facts.reachable_state_refs excludes CollisionAvoidanceSystem/collision_avoidance_deactive/collision_avoidance_active/UnspecifiedInitial; verify_facts.non_proved reachability check for state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:67 status=refuted.
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidanceSystem, as the operating scope required to carry out the collision-avoidance behavior described across NL12/NL13, must be reachable from the machine root so the required substates and transitions can execute at runtime.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM's only root-level transition is '[*] -> AutonomousMode : /Autonomous_mode_start;'; there is no path from the root to CollisionAvoidanceSystem. inspection_equivalent_facts marks CollisionAvoidanceSystem reachable_from_initial=false (diagnostic STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL, line 67) and verify_facts refutes reachability:state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:67.
issues.reason: This is a global root-reachability defect distinct from the narrower malformed owner-local initial-entry defect; the entire operating scope required by NL12/NL13 cannot execute.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met...
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue CollisionAvoidanceSystem is an independently-operating top-level region running in parallel with AutonomousMode and that PlantUML's flat sibling-composite syntax does not require an explicit root transition for every top-level state; but the exact closed FCSTM and its deterministic reachability computation both model a single-entry hierarchy rooted at '[*] -> AutonomousMode' only, so under the model actually being tested this composite and all its behavior are unreachable regardless of author diagram layout intent.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem composite scope is unreachable from the machine root

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers entry for event pedestrian_detected_dist_to_rear_5_vel_30_dist_to_front_15_in_hwy_mode_or_10_in_urban_mode (declared_ref=event:...:line:15) with empty reachable_consumer_transition_refs/state_refs; verify_facts.non_proved check_id event-consumer:pedestrian_detected... status=refuted, subject_refs=['transition:line:72'].
issues.expected: The declared consumer transition (collision_avoidance_deactive -> collision_avoidance_active) for this event must be reachable at runtime so the required collision-avoidance response actually occurs.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers for this exact event shows consumer_transition_refs=['transition:line:72'] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] and reachable_consumer_state_refs=[]; verify_facts refutes event-consumer:pedestrian_detected_dist_to_rear_5_vel_30_dist_to_front_15_in_hwy_mode_or_10_in_urban_mode.
issues.reason: Declared consumer presence is a supporting structural fact but does not satisfy the stronger reachable-consumer coverage obligation; this failure is caused by CollisionAvoidanceSystem's own root-unreachability, but per frontier discipline the consumer-coverage property must still receive its own candidate.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The transition itself is correctly declared with the exact guard/event and correct endpoints, so one could claim the NL obligation (endpoint existence) is satisfied; however the stronger operational-coverage property that this event's response must actually be able to fire is a distinct property from mere declaration, and the exact deterministic facts show zero reachable consumers, which is not discharged by declaration alone.
issues.title: Collision-detection event's consumer transition is declared but never reachable within CollisionAvoidanceSystem

response.basis: Reviewed all 13 numbered NL segments (NL1-NL13) against the primary typed plan's 38 contracts and 8 transition groups. Cross-checked containment obligations against the discourse-continuity rule for sibling operating alternatives under one common enclosing owner (AutonomousMode, HighwayMode, UrbanMode, CollisionAvoidanceSystem) and found each sibling substate introduced by a transition-endpoint clause lacked its own containment row in the primary plan, even where the group or endpoint contract existed. No ledger, score, or evaluation artifact was consulted; only the supplied numbered NL text and primary plan structure were used.
response.reason: The primary plan captured initial-entry, endpoint, guard, termination, and cardinality-relevant obligations thoroughly but systematically omitted many explicit substate containment relations that NL establishes alongside transition endpoints: (a) HighwayMode/UrbanMode as siblings under AutonomousMode (NL2), (b) cruise/lane_change as substates of HighwayMode (NL3), (c) lane_change_urban/straight/intersection as substates of UrbanMode (NL7), (d) exit_urban as a substate of UrbanMode first introduced in NL8, and (e) collision_avoidance_deactive/collision_avoidance_active as substates of the collision avoidance owner scope (NL12). Per the containment-preservation rule, a clause that both transitions into and structurally introduces a substate requires an independent containment contract even though endpoint/initial-entry contracts already exist for the same clause, and covered-segment status does not excuse omitting these. I also added one element_declaration contract for AutonomousMode itself as the root-level operating scope, since its existence as a distinct declared element is independently violable and was not directly represented by any primary contract (only its initial-entry and its containment of InitialState were captured). No new transition groups, endpoint, guard, event-consumer, action, or cardinality obligations were found beyond what the primary plan already represents; alternative destinations, guards, and lifecycle/termination properties for existing transitions are already fully covered by the primary contracts and its transition_groups.
